title: Smoothness at a prime and the singular ideal H_{A/R}
statement: Let $R\to A$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings. For $g\in A$ let $A_g=S^{-1}A$, $S=\{1,g,g^2,\dots\}$, be the localization at $g$, an $R$-algebra. For a prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset A$, the ring map $R\to A$ is *smooth at $\mathfrak q$* if there is $g\in A\setminus\mathfrak q$ such that $A_g$ is a smooth $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] (Algebra, Definition 00TB). Let $G=\{g\in A: A_g\text{ is a smooth }R\text{-algebra}\}$. The *singular ideal of $A$ over $R$* is $H_{A/R}=\sqrt{(G)}\subset A$, the radical of the ideal generated by $G$. Its zero locus $V(H_{A/R})=\bigcap_{g\in G}V(g)$ is the set of primes $\mathfrak q\subset A$ at which $R\to A$ is not smooth, and $H_{A/R}$ is the unique radical ideal with this zero locus (a radical ideal is the intersection of the primes containing it), which is how Stacks defines it.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Definition Tag 07C5 (definition-singular-ideal) in Section 07C4 (section-singular-ideal), with the remark after it that the smooth locus is open by Algebra, Definition Tag 00TB (definition-smooth-at-prime, literature/stacks-project/algebra.tex)
